result.title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
result.summary: Reliable driving VLMs must do more than answer correctly or localize relevant scene actors: they must determine whether the available visual evidence is sufficient to support an answer. Existing evaluations largely treat grounding and answerability as separate measurements, making it difficult to distinguish well-supported predictions from those localized to relevant but insufficient evidence. We introduce DriveAnswer, a benchmark of 20,151 questions across seven reasoning families, that operationalizes this distinction using matched strong- and weak-evidence configurations. Each pair preserves the underlying scene fact and semantic answer while changing whether the observations support answering, making abstention the appropriate response under weak evidence. On the six-family evaluation, the strongest zero-shot baseline reaches 67.31% strong-evidence accuracy, yet only 21.55% of matched questions satisfy both answer-abstain behavior and complete grounding. With controlled adaptation, Gemma-4-12B reaches 63.29% on this joint capability, nearly tripling its zero-shot performance. Qwen3-VL-8B exhibits the same broad improvement in evidence-sensitive answering and grounding. These results show that semantic correctness, evidence sufficiency, and grounding are distinct capabilities that should be evaluated jointly.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DriveAnswer 基准（20,151 题、七个推理族），用保持语义答案不变、仅改变观测是否足以支撑回答的强/弱证据配对，要求模型在弱证据下弃答，并联合评价答案正确性与 grounding。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的证据筛选和停止决策直接相关，「语义正确但证据不足」的配对设计可供核查内部状态是否编码证据充分性、以及定位与弃答是否应共享同一判断。
